resources.string: This phone joined with a network key.
Anyone with the same key can join too, so keep it private.
To join, you need the network key.
You get it from a device that is already in the network: it is the same network key your computer uses to run EdgeVPN.
Other devices reach this phone here.
What the app has been doing, step by step.

This phone will forget the network and become a new device. Your other devices may show the old phone as a separate, unreachable device for a few minutes. You\'ll need the network key to join again.

resources.string: Something went wrong while starting the VPN.
The VPN needs your permission to start.
Map of your devices: %1$d reachable, %2$d offline
At least one of your devices can be reached from this phone right now.
The edgevpn node is running and has an open libp2p connection to at least one peer listed in the network\'s machines ledger.
The VPN is on, but none of your devices has been reached yet. On mobile data this can take a few minutes.
The node is running and searching the public DHT for peers under the network\'s rendezvous point, and listening for mDNS on Wi-Fi. No machine in the ledger has an open connection yet.
Your devices can\'t reach this phone, and it can\'t reach them.
No edgevpn node is running and no VPN interface exists.
The VPN could not start, or stopped because of an error.
The exact error, as returned by the step that failed.
The address your other devices use to reach this phone inside your network.
The IPv4 address of the phone\'s VPN (TUN) interface, announced in the machines ledger.
How this phone is connected to the internet right now.
The transport of the active underlying network, from Android\'s ConnectivityManager.
The devices that have joined your network with the same network key.
Entries of the machines bucket in the edgevpn ledger, which every node keeps a copy of and syncs over GossipSub.
This phone and the device talk straight to each other. This is the fastest way.
At least one open libp2p connection to the peer is not relayed (no /p2p-circuit in the remote multiaddr) and not limited.

Your phone and the device can\'t reach each other directly, usually because both are behind a home router or a mobile network. Their traffic passes through another computer on the internet that offered to help. It works, but it is slower, and the helper may limit how long the connection lasts.

The connection is a libp2p circuit relay v2 connection (the multiaddr contains /p2p-circuit). Relays usually limit these (default: 2 minutes, 128 KiB). libp2p tries hole punching (DCUtR) to upgrade to a direct connection.
The device is in your network but can\'t be reached right now. It may be switched off or without internet.
The peer is in the machines ledger but there is no open libp2p connection to it. \"Last seen\" comes from its last health check in the ledger.
Same Wi-Fi or over the internet
Whether the device is on the same local network as this phone.
Same Wi-Fi means the remote IP of the direct connection is a private address in the same subnet as one of the phone\'s Wi-Fi addresses. Otherwise the connection goes over the internet.
How well this phone can find your devices on the internet.
Discovery uses the public libp2p DHT (Kademlia) and, on Wi-Fi, mDNS.
Other computers on the internet this phone is talking to. They help your devices find each other and can pass traffic along when a direct connection is impossible.
Number of connected libp2p peers that are not machines of the network: DHT servers, relays and bootstrap nodes.
How long ago any of your devices last checked in.
The newest health check timestamp written to the ledger by another node (edgevpn\'s Alive service, every 2 minutes).
The secret that lets devices join your network. Anyone who has it can join, so keep it private.

The edgevpn network token: base64-encoded YAML holding the room name, the rendezvous string, two OTP keys (one rotates the DHT rendezvous point, one encrypts the messages between nodes), the mDNS service name and the maximum message size.
What your other devices see as this phone\'s name.
The Hostname field of this phone\'s entry in the machines ledger.
The address your other devices use to reach this phone inside your network.
The IPv4 address of the phone\'s VPN (TUN) interface, announced in the machines ledger. The VPN routes the address with a /24 mask through the tunnel.
Writes much more detail to the logs, to help find problems. Uses more battery, so turn it off when done.
Sets the edgevpn log level to debug and the libp2p log level to debug. libp2p\'s lines go to logcat (tag GoLog), not to the in-app logs.
A unique identifier for this phone in your network.
The libp2p peer ID, derived from the phone\'s Ed25519 identity key. It signs this phone\'s ledger entries.
Makes this phone forget everything and start over as a new device.

Deletes the network token, the Ed25519 identity key (so a new peer ID is generated) and all settings and logs. The old ledger entries stay owned by the old identity until the ownership TTL (8 minutes) expires.
